title: High Court extends Abhishek Banerjee's protection to 29 January, calls his posts 'painful'
dek: Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya said the Trinamool MP's social-media criticism of the court did not justify ending relief while he cooperates with the police.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Calcutta High Court on Friday extended Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee's protection from arrest and other coercive action until 29 January, saying his recent social-media posts criticising the court were "painful" but were not a reason to refuse him relief while he was cooperating with the police investigation.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya also asked the state to file a report on the progress of the investigation, and directed Mr Banerjee's lawyers to file an affidavit by Monday, according to reports of the hearing.

## What the court said

The case concerns remarks Mr Banerjee made at rallies before this year's Assembly elections. The complainant says his speeches incited opposition workers and threatened Union Home Minister Amit Shah; at a 7 April roadshow he said he would "see who comes to save them on May 4" and referred to a "godfather" in Delhi, according to reports. Mr Banerjee has asked the court to quash the case. He was first granted interim protection on 21 May, on condition that he cooperate with the investigation, and it has been extended several times since.

On Friday Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Mazumder, for the state, argued that Mr Banerjee had repeatedly attacked the High Court and the judiciary on social media, and that this justified ending his protection. Mr Banerjee's lawyer said he was not aware of any derogatory posts and would look into it, according to reports.

The judge said the posts were disturbing and asked why Mr Banerjee was harming his own position. "If an MP is making such statement then what message is sent to his follower?" he asked. But he also asked whether a post could be the basis of contumacious contempt, and whether comments about the judiciary could be grounds to deny an extension. "Today this court doesn't find any alteration of situation requiring refusal to extend interim order," he said, according to reports. The court found nothing to show that Mr Banerjee had failed to cooperate.

## Background

The posts followed the High Court's refusal on Thursday to grant interim protection to Mr Banerjee's aide Sumit Roy in four criminal cases. In a post on X after that order, Mr Banerjee wrote that justice could not be the ruling party's "private privilege" while the opposition fought for its constitutional rights.

The Trinamool Congress, which lost power in this year's Assembly elections, is now in opposition in West Bengal, where the BJP's Suvendu Adhikari is chief minister. The party has accused the state government of using the police against its leaders; the government says the law is taking its course. Neither party had issued a formal statement on the order by Friday evening.

## What happens next

Mr Banerjee's affidavit is due on Monday, and the state must report on the investigation. His protection lasts until 29 January unless the court changes it. One report gave the date as 27 January; most reports and legal outlets said 29 January.
